content.title: 2026 Masters odds on Wednesday, predictions, tee times at Augusta National
content.text: Updated April 8, 2026, 12:03 p.m. ETThe 2026 Masters Tournament arrives Thursday as the pomp and circumstance and flourish that is Augusta National Golf Club has been on display for the past three days.Tens of thousands of patrons have walked the grounds Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday morning, and everyone converges on the Par 3 Course on Wednesday afternoon for a fun-filled afternoon of exhibition golf.But spring is definitely in the air in Eastern Georgia (so is the pollen), which means everyone wants to know who's gonna be putting on a green jacket Sunday evening.Defending champion Rory McIlroy's dream victory a year ago is now officially history. And there are plenty of people ready to become a household name with a title this week.Here's a look at the tournament odds, as well as predictions from USA TODAY Network staff who are covering (and have covered) this tournament over the past two decades.When is the 2026 Masters?The 2026 Masters Tournament kicks off on Thursday, April 9. The final round is scheduled for Sunday, April 12.Tee times for the first two rounds will be released Tuesday.2026 Masters First Round Tee Times(First time is Thursday tee time, second time is Friday tee time)* Amateur participant7:25 a.m. Gary Player, Jack Nicklaus, Tom Watson (honorary starters)7:40 a.m. 10:51 a.m. John Keefer, Haotong Li7:50 a.m. 11:03 a.m. Naoyuki Kataoka, Max Homa, Carlos Ortiz8:02 a.m. 11:15 a.m. Jose Maria Olazabal, Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen, Aldrich Potgieter8:14 a.m. 11:27 a.m. Angel Cabrera, Sami Valimaki, *Jackson Herrington8:26 a.m. 11:39 a.m. Charl Schwartzel, Max Greyserman, Ryan Fox8:38 a.m. 11:51 a.m. Vijay Singh, Matt McCarty, Rasmus Hojgaard8:50 a.m. 12:03 p.m. Kurt Kitayama, Kristoffer Reitan, Casey Jarvis9:02 a.m. 12:15 p.m. Bubba Watson, Nicolas Echavarria, *Brandon Holtz9:19 a.m. 12:32 p.m. Cameron Smith, Sam Burns, Jake Knapp9:31 a.m. 12:44 p.m. Keegan Bradley, Ryan Gerard, Nick Taylor9:43 a.m. 12:56 p.m. Dustin Johnson, Shane Lowry, Jason Day9:55 a.m. 1:08 p.m. Patrick Reed, Tommy Fleetwood, Akshay Bhatia10:07 a.m. 1:20 p.m. Bryson DeChambeau, Matt Fitzpatrick, Xander Schauffele10:19 a.m. 1:32 p.m. Hideki Matsuyama, Collin Morikawa, Russell Henley10:31 a.m. 1:44 p.m. Rory McIlroy, Cameron Young, *Mason Howell10:43 a.m. 1:56 p.m. Viktor Hovland, Patrick Cantlay, Alex Noren11:03 a.m. 7:40 a.m. Samuel Stevens, Sungjae Im11:15 a.m. 7:50 a.m. Andrew Novak, Tom McKibbin, Brian Campbell11:27 a.m. 8:02 a.m. Mike Weir, Wyndham Clark, *Mateo Pulcini11:39 a.m. 8:14 a.m. Zach Johnson, Michael Kim, Nicolai Hojgaard11:51 a.m. 8:26 a.m. Danny Willett, Davis Riley, *Ethan Fang12:03 p.m. 8:38 a.m. Adam Scott, Daniel Berger, Brian Harman12:15 p.m. 8:50 a.m. Fred Couples, Min Woo Lee, *Fifa Laopakdee12:27 p.m. 9:02 a.m. Sergio Garcia, Aaron Rai, Jacob Bridgeman12:44 p.m. 9:19 a.m. Harry Hall, Corey Conners, Michael Brennan12:56 p.m. 9:31 a.m. J.J. The first time is for their first round Thursday, the second time is for their second round Friday.9:55 a.m. 1:08 p.m. Patrick Reed, Tommy Fleetwood, Akshay Bhatia10:07 a.m. 1:20 p.m. Bryson DeChambeau, Matt Fitzpatrick, Xander Schauffele10:19 a.m. 1:32 p.m. Hideki Matsuyama, Collin Morikawa, Russell Henley1:08 p.m. 9:43 a.m. Jon Rahm, Chris Gotterup, Ludvig Aberg1:20 p.m. 9:55 a.m. Jordan Spieth, Justin Rose, Brooks Koepka1:44 p.m. 10:19 a.m. Scottie Scheffler, Robert MacIntyre, Gary Woodland2026 Masters Odds on WednesdayOdds courtesy of BetMGM.com as of Wednesday afternoonScottie Scheffler +600Jon Rahm +1000Bryson DeChambeau +1200Rory McIlroy +1200Xander Schauffele +1400Ludvig Aberg +1400Cameron Young +2000Matthew Fitzpatrick +2200Tommy Fleetwood +2200Hideki Matsuyama +2800Collin Morikawa +3000Justin Rose +3000Robert MacIntyre +3000Min Woo Lee +3300Patrick Reed +3300Brooks Koepka +4000Jordan Spieth +4000Viktor Hovland +4000Chris Gotterup +4500Si Woo Kim +50002026 Masters predictions and picks for the winnerWill Cheney, Augusta Chronicle staff and USA TODAY sports content coachWho's Gonna Win: Justin Rose (in a playoff, perhaps). He's lost in a pair of Masters playoffs (Sergio Garcia in 2017 and Rory McIlroy in 2025). Experience plays here and this will be his 21st start at Augusta. It would only be fitting to see McIlroy put the green jacket on Rose early Sunday evening; playoff, or no playoff.Who's Gonna Be A Surprise (Good or Bad): Ben Griffin was consistently good from April through the end of 2025, earning victories at the Zurich Classic (with fellow ’26 Masters invitee Andrew Novak), the Charles Schwab Challenge and the World Wide Technology Championship (with a 72-hole scoring record). He’s due to make some noise in his first start at Augusta.Biggest name to miss the cut: Jordan Spieth. The 2015 Masters champion owns one of the hottest starts to a career in the tournament’s history with top-two finishes in his first three starts. Spieth’s time at Augusta National has been feast-or-famine of late. Since 2021, he’s finished in the top five twice and missed the cut just as many times.Dhani Joseph, Augusta Chronicle sports reporterWho's Gonna Win: Only three golfers in Masters history have won it back-to-back times: Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo and Tiger Woods. I think Rory McIlroy will be the next up to do that after breaking through a year ago.Who's Gonna Be A Surprise (Good or Bad): Xander Schauffele will fall out of the top 10, a place where he's been in five out of the last seven starts here.Biggest name to miss the cut: Despite being one of the hotter players coming into the tournament Si Woo Kim will just barely miss the cut in his ninth start.Ryne Dennis: USA TODAY Deep South Connect team editor, former Athens Banner-Herald sports editorWho's Gonna Win: Bryson DeChambeau has six top-10 finishes in his last eight majors and is clearly the best player of late on the LIV tour. It feels like he's ready to take the next step in his professional career.Who's Gonna Be A Surprise (Good or Bad): Scottie Scheffler and Rory McIlroy won't finish in the top 10. The two former champions haven't been at the top of their game of late. Scottie hasn't gotten off to fast starts this season, and Rory has been dealing with a tweak in his back. While Scheffler has rallied to a win and grab a pair of top-four finishes, his results have declined as the season has progressed. And if Rory's back is still an issue, I wouldn't trust it at a grueling Augusta National.Biggest name to miss the cut: Justin Thomas. Still trying to find consistency after offseason surgery on his lower back. He's missed the cut in two of three Masters, and only had a T-36 showing last year.Dan Spears: USA TODAY Network sports strategist, former Augusta Chronicle night sports editorWho's Gonna Win: Ludvig Aberg. The swinging Swede is 2-for-2 on being in contention at Augusta National and, in a year with no true favorite (or even sentimental favorite), he's got the confidence here to win a major championship despite having a terrible track record in the other three slam events early in his career.Who's Gonna Be A Surprise (Good or Bad): The Masters never disappoints, but this year the green jacket will be a fight among players without majors, or maybe one at most: Aberg, Matt Fitzpatrick, Tommy Fleetwood, Ben Griffin, Chris Gotterup, Cam Young.Biggest name to miss the cut: Russell Henley didn't play the weekend here a year ago and, despite five top-20 finishes in six starts so far in 2026, it will be another early trip home for the U.S. Ryder Cupper.
